convert() collapses ', ,' → ',' as its last rule, so if the same string is swept twice you can get punctuation drift — safe for now but worth noting for future re-runs.

Only outstanding items are the `—`-HTML-entity leftovers in SocialProofStrip.jsx / FacultySection.jsx and DB-sourced em dashes in course catalog descriptions. No JS/console errors observed on landing, /login, /signup, /courses, /admin-panel, or /dashboard.
rca of the issue: strip_em_dashes.py operates on raw file text and only checks for the literal em-dash character (U+2014). It does not match HTML entity encodings (—, —). Files that use JSX entity form (SocialProofStrip.jsx, FacultySection.jsx) were therefore untouched, and the em dashes still render in the browser. Mitigation: add `text = text.replace('—', ', ').replace('—', ', ')` before the regex passes, or run a follow-up JSX-aware pass. Also, DB rows in Supabase course_paths/roles carry em dashes that a file sweep cannot reach — needs a SQL migration if desired.
